Let me preface this with, I am not a hiring manager myself (in my current role). But, I have been a program coordinator in another industry. In addition to the things that have been mentioned, there were a couple of things that I looked for in potential team members:

1 – General interest for the field in general. For programmers, one indicator of this would be working on projects outside of their normal job. I’ve worked with plenty of very smart people who were competent, but not particularly interested, in their jobs. My experience is that they become very smart people who turn in mediocre work.

2 – A healthy interest in other hobbies not related to the task at hand. Well rounded people seem to have a larger base of experience to draw from in coming up with solutions to interesting problems.

3 – Active leadership in trade organizations (user groups, etc.) generally indicates overall leadership qualities and initiative. Active leadership in other organizations is good as well.

In my experience, overall character and personality can easily seperate a “great employee” from a “good worker.” Beyond being technically proficient, to be a great hire someone must be a good team player that can lead, follow, and generally work well with others.

Just my 2 cents.
